title: History and Documentation Optimization in Urology using a Conversational Large Language Model
summary: In urology outpatient clinics, high patient volumes and limited staffing often leave little time for a comprehensive medical history, even though it forms a crucial basis for diagnosis and treatment. This study investigates whether a voice-based software application running on a tablet can conduct a structured interview with patients about their symptoms while they are waiting for their consultation. Based on the patient’s responses, the application automatically generates a clear, structured, and immediately usable summary, which is provided to the treating physician as documentation. The system does not establish diagnoses, provide treatment recommendations, or replace the physician–patient consultation. The study compares whether this pre-consultation support leads to a more complete documentation of the patient’s medical history and whether it significantly reduces the time physicians spend on documentation. In addition, the study evaluates patient satisfaction with the system and assesses whether physicians perceive the workflow as reducing their workload.

interventions.name: Emergency patients presenting to the urology outpatient clinic complete a digital medical history interview with a purpose-built large language model (LLM) before the physician-conducted medical history is obtained.

Emergency patients presenting to the urology outpatient clinic do not undergo a digital medical history interview prior to physician-led history taking. Medical history is obtained exclusively during the physician-conducted medical history interview.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Ability to provide informed consent and presentation to the outpatient urology clinic with acute urological complaints (e.g., flank pain, gross hematuria, etc.)
Exclusion criteria:
Cognitive impairment or psychiatric disorders that preclude the provision of informed consent; insufficient proficiency in the German language.
